slides.text: Your AI agents now have a <accent>virtual office.</accent> A free VS Code extension that turns your coding agents into <accent>animated pixel art characters.</accent> They walk, sit at desks, and react to what your agent is <accent>actually doing.</accent>

slides.heading: The <accent>Problem</accent>
slides.body:
- You fire up Claude Code in the background
- Just a blinking cursor and scrolling text
- Zero visual feedback on what the agent is doing
- No way to know if it's stuck or making progress
- Reading terminal logs is painful

slides.text: What if you could actually watch your AI agents work? Not read logs. Watch them.

slides.heading: Install in <accent>30 Seconds</accent>
slides.body:
- Search 'Pixel Agents' in VS Code
- Or install from command line
- Open with Cmd+Shift+P
- Click +Agent to spawn characters

slides.heading: Meet the <accent>Characters</accent>
slides.caption: Six unique pixel art characters, each representing a different coding agent

slides.heading: This Is the <accent>Office</accent>
slides.caption: Your AI agents sit at desks, walk around, and work in a pixel art office in real time

slides.heading: Why Devs <accent>Love</accent> It
items: Visual feedback without reading terminal logs
Covered by Fast Company, trending on GitHub
Build custom offices with 64x64 grid editor

slides.heading: The <accent>Bigger</accent> Picture
slides.body:
- AI agents are becoming teammates, not tools
- Visualizing their work builds trust
- Gives you instant feedback on agent state
- This is just the beginning of human-AI interaction
- The future of coding is spectator-friendly
